recentItems.title: Edmonton man charged in Sikh temple stabbing three weeks after attack | Hanomansing Tonight
recentItems.description:
An Edmonton man has been charged three weeks after two men were stabbed inside a local Sikh temple. Police said Austin Sim-Pelletier, 27, has been charged with two counts of assault causing bodily harm, one count of possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose and one count of mischief. The accused was granted statutory release from federal prison the day before the attack.

recentItems.title: Edmonton Oilers can't be surprised by criticism for Formenton deal: journalist | Hanomansing Tonight
recentItems.description:
The Edmonton Oilers stepped into a wave of controversy Wednesday when they signed Alex Formenton to a one-year contract. Formenton was one of five players from Canada's 2018 world junior team charged with sexual assault in connection with an encounter with a woman after a Hockey Canada gala in London, Ont. He was acquitted last year. Former The Athletic writer Daniel Nugent-Bowman says Formenton's actions weren't 'a mistake.'

recentItems.title: Canadian whey protein products caught in Canada-U.S. trade war | Hanomansing Tonight
recentItems.description:

Dan Crosby, CEO of BioSteel Sports Nutrition, explains how this ban will impact his company's products, which are popular with sports teams and players on both sides of the border.

recentItems.title: Could Canadian tariffs swing votes in U.S. midterm elections? | Power & Politics
recentItems.description:
While Democratic governors warn of the 'catastrophic' economic impacts of U.S. President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada, Trump promises each voting-age American a $5,000 US 'dividend' if Republicans retain control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections. Power & Politics hears from Chuck Todd, former host of NBC's Meet the Press and current host of the Chuck ToddCast, on what it could all mean as Americans head to the polls in November.

recentItems.title: What is New Brunswick doing to combat tariff fallout? | Power & Politics
recentItems.description:

Power & Politics speaks with New Brunswick Premier Susan Holt about what her province is doing to promote buying Canadian.

recentItems.title: Ontario premier shuffles cabinet after resignations of 3 key ministers over the summer
recentItems.description:
Ontario Premier Doug Ford is overhauling his cabinet and adding a new artificial intelligence portfolio. Ford says the changes are to help protect the province during the tariff dispute with the U.S., and include shuffling the embattled David Piccini from the labour portfolio to infrastructure. Piccini is currently under investigation over mishandling of funds.

recentItems.description:
